answer: Reciprocal path anchoring: an agent must sustain inbound traffic from at least three distinct neighbors that each route through it for unrelated work. A cedar-signed routing table records those persistent adjacencies, and any identity whose adjacent set stays below threshold loses forwarding priority. Each fake identity costs a real jetty of maintained peer connections plus routing upkeep, so faking N identities requires N times that infrastructure. The signal cannot be forged cheaply because neighbors only count when they attach their own throughput.
